properties.title: BluePeak Consulting Electrifies Its Brussels Office with NX-100 Charging
properties.customerChallenge: BluePeak Consulting, a 45-person boutique management consultancy in Brussels, wanted to offer EV charging for its small leadership team and visiting client vehicles without the capital outlay or complexity of a large charging infrastructure project. Their single-building office had only 14 dedicated parking spaces and no existing dedicated three-phase supply beyond standard office electrical service.
properties.solution: NMG recommended the Nova AC 100 (NX-100), a single-socket 7.4kW AC charger requiring no specialized electrical upgrade, deployed across 12 of the 14 parking spaces. Given BluePeak's modest scale and single-site footprint, NMG explicitly steered the client away from higher-tier NX-200/NX-400 units, whose RFID access control and dynamic load balancing capabilities would have added cost with no practical benefit for a 12-space, single-tenant office.
properties.implementation: Installation was completed by a certified NMG installer partner over a single weekend, with no requirement for a dedicated transformer or three-phase supply upgrade since the NX-100 operates on standard building power. BluePeak staff self-registered charging sessions via a simple mobile web link; no Polaris Charge Cloud subscription was needed given the absence of billing or multi-site reporting requirements.
properties.results: Within 3 months, 80% of BluePeak's company-car and hybrid-driving staff were charging on-site at least twice weekly, and the firm reported a measurable increase in employee satisfaction scores tied to workplace amenities. Total project cost stayed within BluePeak's original budget envelope, avoiding any need for electrical infrastructure upgrades.
properties.customerQuote: “We didn't need a fleet-grade charging platform — we needed reliable, simple chargers our people could use every day without a support ticket. NX-100 was exactly right-sized for us,” said Elke Van Damme, Head of Operations at BluePeak Consulting.
properties.lessonsLearned: The engagement reinforced that right-sizing matters as much for a small office as for a large campus: recommending the simplest capable product, rather than defaulting to a feature-rich unit, produced a faster sale, a faster install, and a more satisfied customer.

properties.title: Veridian Foods Centralizes Charging Across Its Munich Headquarters Campus
properties.customerChallenge: Veridian Foods' Munich headquarters campus hosts over 900 employees plus regular supplier and client visitors, and the company's own light commercial vehicle fleet used for regional distribution. Existing charging (a handful of first-generation units) could not report usage by department, had no RFID access control, and left facilities management unable to answer basic questions about who was charging and how much energy was consumed.
properties.solution: NMG proposed a mixed campus deployment: NX-200 units for standard employee parking bays and NX-400 units, with RFID access and dynamic load balancing, concentrated near the main entrance and reserved fleet bays where higher utilization and access control mattered most. Polaris Charge Cloud was added for centralized device management, driver management, and reporting across the whole campus from a single dashboard.
properties.implementation: Deployment was phased over 5 months to avoid disrupting campus operations, starting with the fleet-bay NX-400 units (which required a dedicated three-phase supply upgrade coordinated with Veridian's facilities team) and finishing with the broader employee-parking NX-200 rollout. Polaris Charge Cloud was configured with RFID-based cost allocation so facilities could report charging costs back to individual departments.
properties.results: Facilities management gained full visibility into charging usage for the first time, with automated monthly reports replacing a previously manual, spreadsheet-based estimate. Fleet-vehicle charging reliability improved, and dynamic load balancing on the NX-400 units allowed Veridian to add charging capacity without exceeding the campus's existing electrical service capacity.
properties.customerQuote: “Polaris Charge Cloud gave us, for the first time, a single place to see exactly how our charging infrastructure is being used across the whole campus,” said Torsten Baumann, Facilities Director at Veridian Foods.
properties.lessonsLearned: A single-site headquarters deployment still benefits from tiered product selection — matching NX-200 to lower-utilization employee bays and reserving NX-400's dynamic load balancing for the highest-traffic, access-controlled areas — rather than a uniform one-size-fits-all approach.
properties.tags: corporate headquarters, NX-400, Polaris Charge Cloud, Germany

properties.title: Ardent Hotels Adds Guest Fast Charging Across 8 Spanish Properties
properties.customerChallenge: Ardent Hotels, an 8-property boutique hotel group across Madrid, Barcelona, and the Costa del Sol, was losing bookings to competing hotels that already advertised EV charging as a guest amenity. Guests increasingly expected fast, reliable charging during an overnight stay, not a slow trickle-charge that couldn't top up a car in the hours available.
properties.solution: NMG recommended DX-60 fast chargers (60kW, single CCS2 gun) at each property's most visible guest parking spots to deliver a meaningful overnight charge quickly, paired with NX-200 units for staff and valet parking where speed mattered less but RFID access control did. This combination avoided the far larger installation footprint and cost of a DX-120/DX-240 deployment that Ardent's guest volume did not justify.
properties.implementation: Installation was staged property by property over 4 months, prioritizing the two flagship Madrid and Barcelona properties first. Spain's Gold-tier service plan extended on-site response time to 10 hours outside the Madrid/Barcelona metro areas, which Ardent's operations team factored into their support planning for the smaller Costa del Sol properties.
properties.results: Guest satisfaction survey scores tied to “hotel amenities” rose measurably in the two quarters following rollout, and Ardent reports that EV charging availability is now cited in a meaningful share of new group and corporate booking inquiries. Average charger uptime across all 8 properties has held above 98% since installation.
properties.customerQuote: “Our guests don't want to wait until morning for a usable charge — DX-60 gives them a real charge during a normal dinner and overnight stay,” said Marisol Fuentes, VP of Guest Experience at Ardent Hotels.
properties.lessonsLearned: For hospitality deployments, matching charger speed to the guest's actual dwell time (an overnight stay) is the deciding factor, not raw power — DX-60 struck the right balance between charge speed and installation cost across a multi-property rollout.

properties.title: Solena Retail Turns Charging Into a Shopper Retention Tool at Its Milan Shopping Center
properties.customerChallenge: Solena Retail's flagship Milan shopping center saw high visitor volume but limited dwell time unless shoppers had a reason to stay longer. Management wanted a charging offering that would both serve high parking-lot traffic reliably and give time-pressed shoppers a genuine fast-charge option during a typical 60-90 minute shopping visit.
properties.solution: NMG proposed a two-tier approach: NX-400 units with dynamic load balancing across the bulk of the parking structure to serve steady all-day AC charging demand without exceeding the center's electrical capacity, plus a smaller bank of DX-120 fast chargers near the main entrance for shoppers who specifically wanted a rapid top-up during their visit.
properties.implementation: The DX-120 fast-charging bank required a dedicated ~175A three-phase supply, coordinated with the center's existing electrical infrastructure during a planned off-season maintenance window to minimize disruption to shoppers. The NX-400 units were rolled out across the remaining structure over the following two months.
properties.results: Solena reports a measurable increase in average shopper dwell time among EV-driving visitors using the DX-120 fast chargers, and dynamic load balancing on the NX-400 fleet has allowed continued expansion of AC charging bays without a further electrical service upgrade. Charger uptime has averaged 97.5% across the full deployment.
properties.customerQuote: “Charging isn't just an amenity for us anymore — it's a reason for an EV-driving shopper to choose our center over a competitor's,” said Giulia Moretti, Center Operations Manager at Solena Retail.
properties.lessonsLearned: A shopping center benefits from segmenting its charging offer by shopper intent — steady AC charging for long visits, fast DC charging for shorter ones — rather than deploying a single uniform charger type across the entire lot.
properties.tags: shopping center, NX-400, DX-120, Italy, retail

properties.title: Greenway Logistics Electrifies Its Lyon Distribution Hub with Modular DC Fast Charging
properties.customerChallenge: Greenway Logistics operates a growing fleet of electric delivery trucks out of its Lyon distribution hub and needed depot charging infrastructure capable of turning around a large vehicle fleet overnight and during shift changes, without exceeding the site's available electrical capacity or requiring a second major substation investment beyond what was already budgeted.
properties.solution: NMG deployed a combination of DX-240 and DX-360 modular DC fast chargers across the depot's truck bays, sized to Greenway's dedicated ~350-400A three-phase supply, alongside Atlas Fleet software for route-aware charge scheduling and depot capacity forecasting so dispatchers could plan overnight charging around next-day delivery routes.
properties.deploymentSize: 180 charging points across 1 logistics distribution hub
properties.implementation: Installation required a dedicated transformer room and substantial cable routing work, completed over a 6-month phased build-out coordinated with Greenway's facilities and electrical contractor. Atlas Fleet's depot capacity forecasting module was configured against Greenway's actual delivery schedules before go-live, allowing dispatch to validate that charging capacity would meet fleet turnaround needs before the full fleet transition was complete.
properties.results: Greenway achieved 92% fleet electrification at the Lyon hub within 14 months of the project's start, with Atlas Fleet's route-aware scheduling reducing overnight charging conflicts by a significant margin compared to the ad hoc scheduling used during the pilot phase. Average charger uptime across the DX-240/DX-360 fleet has remained above 97% since full deployment.
properties.customerQuote: “Atlas Fleet lets our dispatchers see charging capacity the same way they see delivery routes — as one connected planning problem, not two separate ones,” said Nicolas Lambert, Fleet Operations Director at Greenway Logistics.
properties.lessonsLearned: A logistics depot's charging capacity is only as useful as the scheduling intelligence layered on top of it — the DX-240/DX-360 hardware solved the power problem, but Atlas Fleet's forecasting is what made the fleet electrification transition operationally manageable at scale.
properties.tags: logistics fleet, DX-240, DX-360, Atlas Fleet, France

properties.title: Metrovia Services Rolls Out City-Wide Municipal Charging Across Rotterdam
properties.customerChallenge: Metrovia Services, contracted to manage public parking infrastructure for the city of Rotterdam, needed to deploy EV charging at scale across dozens of municipal parking facilities under significant budget scrutiny from city council, while also meeting growing resident demand and the city's own electrification targets.
properties.solution: NMG worked with Metrovia to segment the rollout by facility traffic and budget tier: high-traffic, high-visibility municipal garages received NX-400 units with dynamic load balancing to maximize charging throughput per available electrical connection, while lower-traffic neighborhood parking facilities received the more budget-conscious NX-200, avoiding unnecessary spend on facilities with lighter and less predictable usage.
properties.deploymentSize: 220 charging points across 34 municipal parking facilities
properties.implementation: The city-wide rollout was phased across 18 months by facility priority, with Rotterdam commuter facilities prioritized first. As a Netherlands-based Gold service plan customer, Metrovia's highest-traffic facilities in Rotterdam qualified for the standard 4-hour on-site metro response window, while facilities outside the core metro areas were planned around the 8-hour non-metro response time.
properties.results: Metrovia reports that resident EV charging complaints to the city dropped substantially after full rollout, and dynamic load balancing on the NX-400 facilities allowed the city to avoid several planned electrical service upgrades that would otherwise have been required to support the same charging capacity. The program has since been cited by two neighboring municipalities evaluating similar rollouts.
properties.customerQuote: “We had to prove to city council that this would work at scale and on budget — segmenting by traffic tier instead of deploying one product everywhere is what made the numbers work,” said Bram de Vries, Program Director at Metrovia Services.
properties.lessonsLearned: A budget-constrained, large-scale municipal rollout benefits from explicit traffic-tier segmentation rather than uniform product selection — matching NX-200 to lower-traffic facilities freed budget to deploy NX-400's higher throughput where it was actually needed.
properties.tags: municipal parking, NX-200, NX-400, Netherlands, public sector

properties.title: Lindqvist Property Group Charging Deployment at De Meridiaan Residences (Archived)
properties.customerChallenge: Lindqvist Property Group managed De Meridiaan, a 40-unit apartment building in Utrecht, and wanted to offer residents dedicated EV charging in the building's underground parking garage, with individual billing per resident rather than a shared building cost.
properties.solution: NMG deployed NX-100 units for residents who wanted a dedicated, individually-metered charger and a smaller number of shared NX-200 units with RFID access for residents without a dedicated bay, allowing per-resident billing through RFID-tagged charging sessions.
properties.implementation: Installation was completed over 6 weeks, coordinated with the building's homeowners' association to allocate charger costs fairly between residents who opted in and the shared building infrastructure budget.
properties.results: Resident adoption reached 24 active charging accounts within the first year, and the RFID-based billing model was well received as a fair way to allocate shared charger costs. The deployment served as an early reference for Lindqvist's broader property portfolio.
properties.customerQuote: “Individual billing was the deciding factor for our residents — nobody wanted to subsidize someone else's charging,” said Anouk Jansen, Property Manager at Lindqvist Property Group, at the time of the original deployment.
properties.lessonsLearned: RFID-based per-resident billing was essential to resident acceptance in a shared-building context; a flat building-wide charging cost allocation would likely have faced resistance from non-EV-owning residents. This case study is retained for reference purposes only: Lindqvist's management contract for De Meridiaan ended in late 2025 following the building's sale to a new owner, and NMG's relationship with this specific property has since concluded.
properties.tags: apartment building, NX-100, NX-200, Netherlands, archived

properties.title: Cavallo Mobility Rentals Speeds Up Fleet Turnaround with Mixed AC/DC Charging
properties.customerChallenge: Cavallo Mobility Rentals, operating EV rental fleets out of Rome and Milan airport locations, needed to turn returned rental vehicles around fast enough to meet same-day re-rental demand, while also charging a larger share of the fleet overnight when rental volume was lower.
properties.solution: NMG recommended DX-60 fast chargers for the return-lane bays where quick turnaround mattered most, allowing a returned vehicle to reach a rentable charge level within the time needed for cleaning and inspection, combined with NX-400 units across the main overnight parking area for the bulk of the fleet, where dynamic load balancing let Cavallo charge more vehicles simultaneously without exceeding depot electrical capacity.
properties.deploymentSize: 85 charging points across 2 airport rental locations
properties.implementation: The Rome location was deployed first as a pilot over 3 months, with the Milan location following once Cavallo's operations team had validated the return-lane DX-60 turnaround workflow against real rental volumes.
properties.results: Cavallo reports that same-day EV re-rental availability improved meaningfully after the DX-60 return-lane chargers went live, and overnight NX-400 dynamic load balancing allowed the company to expand its EV rental fleet size without a further electrical service upgrade at either airport location.
properties.customerQuote: “Every minute a car sits in the return lane instead of being re-rented is lost revenue — DX-60 turned that around for us,” said Roberto Ferraro, Fleet Operations Manager at Cavallo Mobility Rentals.
properties.lessonsLearned: A rental fleet's charging needs split cleanly into two distinct use cases — fast return-lane turnaround and steady overnight bulk charging — and matching different NMG products to each use case outperformed a single uniform charger choice.

properties.title: Nordkreuz Parcel Express Cuts Depot Charging Conflicts with DX-240 and Atlas Fleet
properties.customerChallenge: Nordkreuz Parcel Express operates a growing electric last-mile delivery van fleet out of its Frankfurt depot and was experiencing frequent charging conflicts during shift changes, when returning vans and departing vans competed for the same limited charging bays under the depot's existing electrical capacity.
properties.solution: NMG deployed DX-240 modular DC fast chargers sized to the depot's dedicated three-phase supply, paired with Atlas Fleet for route-aware charge scheduling that sequences which vans charge first based on their next assigned route and required range, reducing the shift-change bottleneck that had been the depot's main operational pain point.
properties.implementation: Installation followed the same dedicated transformer room and cable routing pattern used for other DX-240 depot deployments, completed over 3 months. Atlas Fleet's route-aware scheduling was configured against Nordkreuz's actual delivery route data during a 4-week tuning period before full go-live.
properties.results: Shift-change charging conflicts dropped substantially after Atlas Fleet's route-aware scheduling went live, and Nordkreuz reports improved on-time delivery rates as a direct result of vans reliably reaching their required charge level before their assigned route departure time. Fleet electrification at the Frankfurt depot has reached 78% of total delivery vehicles.
properties.customerQuote: “We weren't short on charging power — we were short on charging intelligence. Atlas Fleet solved the actual problem,” said Petra Hoffmann, Depot Operations Lead at Nordkreuz Parcel Express.
properties.lessonsLearned: For a delivery fleet under tight shift-change time pressure, software-driven scheduling can matter as much as raw charger count — Nordkreuz's conflicts were a scheduling problem, not purely a hardware capacity problem.
properties.tags: delivery fleet, DX-240, Atlas Fleet, Germany

properties.title: Voyage Autoroute Services Deploys High-Power Charging at an A6 Highway Rest Stop
properties.customerChallenge: Voyage Autoroute Services operates a rest stop on the A6 highway between Paris and Lyon and needed to offer highway travelers a genuinely fast charge — typically 15-25 minutes — to match the short stop duration travelers were willing to accept, while also managing installation cost given the site's existing electrical infrastructure limitations.
properties.solution: NMG recommended a mix of DX-240 and DX-360 units rather than defaulting entirely to the highest-power DX-360 across the whole site: DX-360's full 360kW modular capacity was reserved for a smaller number of premium bays intended for the fastest possible turnaround, while DX-240 covered the majority of bays at a lower installation cost, since DX-240's 240kW modular capacity still delivered a highway-appropriate fast charge for most vehicles without requiring the largest substation investment across the entire site.
properties.deploymentSize: 32 charging points across 1 highway rest stop
properties.implementation: The site required a dedicated MV/LV substation above 400A given the concentration of DC fast chargers, built out over an 8-month project coordinated with the regional grid operator. Bays were physically arranged to give trucks and larger vehicles clear access to the DX-360 premium bays.
properties.results: Average traveler stop duration at the rest stop has remained within the target 15-25 minute window since full deployment, and Voyage reports the site is now consistently among the highest-utilization highway charging locations in its network. Charger uptime has averaged 96.8% since go-live, with the majority of maintenance events related to the DX-360 bays' higher session volume.
properties.customerQuote: “We didn't need DX-360 on every bay to hit our stop-time targets — the mix NMG recommended got us there for meaningfully less capital cost,” said Camille Rousseau, Network Development Manager at Voyage Autoroute Services.
properties.lessonsLearned: A highway site benefits from a deliberate power mix rather than uniformly deploying the highest-power unit available — DX-240 met the actual traveler stop-time requirement for most bays, and reserving DX-360 for a smaller premium tier controlled overall project cost without compromising the site's fast-charging value proposition.

properties.title: Helios Manufacturing Balances Plant Load and Fleet Charging with Orion Energy Manager
properties.customerChallenge: Helios Manufacturing's Toulouse production plant already ran near the limits of its existing electrical service for manufacturing equipment, and needed to add charging for its growing electric forklift and yard-vehicle fleet plus employee EV parking without triggering a costly electrical service upgrade or risking manufacturing line disruptions from unmanaged charging load spikes.
properties.solution: NMG deployed a mix of DX-120 and DX-240 units across the fleet/forklift charging zone and general employee parking, paired with Orion Energy Manager to dynamically manage total site load — prioritizing manufacturing equipment and charging fleet vehicles only within available headroom, with charging priority rules ensuring fleet vehicles charged ahead of visitor and lower-priority employee vehicles when total demand approached the site's electrical ceiling.
properties.implementation: Orion Energy Manager was configured and tuned against Helios's actual production line load profile over a 6-week period before full charging capacity was activated, ensuring the dynamic load management logic would never compete with manufacturing equipment for available power during peak production shifts.
properties.results: Helios avoided a planned electrical service upgrade that would have been required without Orion Energy Manager's dynamic load balancing, and reports a measurable reduction in peak demand charges on its electricity bill since full deployment, as charging load is now actively shifted away from the plant's existing peak-demand windows.
properties.customerQuote: “Orion Energy Manager is the only reason we could add this much charging capacity without a multi-million-euro electrical upgrade,” said Jean-Marc Petit, Plant Engineering Director at Helios Manufacturing.
properties.lessonsLearned: For an industrial site already near its electrical capacity limit, dynamic energy management software is not optional — it is what makes fleet electrification financially and operationally viable without a disruptive infrastructure upgrade.
properties.tags: industrial facility, DX-240, Orion Energy Manager, France

properties.title: Continental Facilities Group Standardizes Charging Across Four Countries with Polaris and Orion
properties.industry: Commercial real estate and facilities management (multi-country enterprise)
properties.customerChallenge: Continental Facilities Group manages commercial office and mixed-use properties across its Brussels headquarters plus regional operations in France, Germany, and the Netherlands, and needed a single, centrally-manageable charging standard across dozens of properties with widely varying site power availability, traffic patterns, and country-specific service expectations, rather than a patchwork of vendor and product choices site-by-site.
properties.solution: NMG proposed a segmented but centrally-managed approach: NX-200 and NX-400 for the majority of standard office and mixed-use properties, DX-120 for a smaller number of high-traffic flagship properties, and NX-450 selectively deployed at premium flagship sites where Plug & Charge and improved energy metering justified the premium tier — all unified under Polaris Charge Cloud for centralized device management, billing, and reporting across all four countries, with Orion Energy Manager layered in at sites with existing high building loads or on-site solar generation.
properties.productsUsed: NX-200, NX-400, NX-450, DX-120, Polaris Charge Cloud, Orion Energy Manager
properties.deploymentSize: 410 charging points across 47 properties in 4 countries
properties.implementation: The rollout was phased by country over 22 months, starting with the Belgium headquarters properties, then France, Germany, and finally the Netherlands, with each country's deployment respecting local service-plan nuances — including Germany's Bavaria/Baden-Württemberg same-day Professional-plan exception and the Netherlands' Amsterdam/Rotterdam/Utrecht/The Hague Gold-tier metro coverage. Polaris Charge Cloud's API Management module was used to integrate charging data into Continental's existing facilities management platform.
properties.results: Continental achieved a single, centrally-reported view of charging utilization, cost, and uptime across all four countries for the first time, and reports a significant reduction in peak demand charges across its Orion Energy Manager-equipped properties. Average charger uptime across the full 410-point deployment has held above 97% since the rollout's completion.
properties.customerQuote: “Before this program, every country ran its own version of ‘the charging vendor.’ Now we have one platform, one reporting standard, and one relationship,” said Sophie Lefebvre, VP of Facilities Technology at Continental Facilities Group.
properties.lessonsLearned: A multi-country enterprise rollout succeeds when the underlying hardware selection is allowed to vary by site while the management layer — Polaris Charge Cloud and, where needed, Orion Energy Manager — stays centrally standardized; forcing identical hardware everywhere would have meant either overpaying at low-traffic sites or under-provisioning high-traffic ones.
properties.relatedProducts: NX-200, NX-400, NX-450, DX-120, Polaris Charge Cloud, Orion Energy Manager
properties.tags: multi-country enterprise, Polaris Charge Cloud, Orion Energy Manager, global
